method.build: All benchmark binaries were rebuilt using static/build.sh with the pinned compiler archive.
method.sync: Synchronization logic is unchanged from a43e5f9; no preallocation is used.
method.micro: 512 MiB fully allocated fixture on tmpfs; direct frontend I/O; warm backing-file cache; three samples of three seconds per workload.
method.fat: Fresh regular FAT32 loop images on ext4, 32 KiB clusters, identical input contents, alternating variant order, three repetitions.
method.integrity: Compare file contents after remounting XFS, dynfilefs and FAT32; timestamps and other metadata are excluded from SHA-256.
method.allocation: Sum storage-part st_blocks times 512 after synchronization; the main metadata file is excluded.
method.tracing: Separate 16 MiB write and read with 128 KiB requests, excluded from timings.

limitations: Earlier FAT runs affected by HostMemoryLow or temporary cgroup limits were discarded.
The VM was restarted with 18 GiB. Ample host memory and zero guest memory-pressure events did not eliminate VirtualBox timer catch-up warnings.
FAT32 timing medians are exploratory. Large-file copy ranges overlap widely; these data do not establish a reliable disk-write speedup.
The first post-restart baseline microbenchmark stalled. A complete baseline rerun at the end is provided separately; no samples were removed from either run.
Pre-restart tmpfs runs are retained as preliminary results and are not the headline baseline.
These are VM loop-image and warm-cache measurements, not physical USB or cold-drive throughput.
512 KiB blocks amplify spaced 4 KiB writes from 5.41 MiB to 500.50 MiB on FAT32.
validation: Full pinned 32-bit static/build.sh passed for the intermediate and final versions.
32-bit musl callback tests passed: ENOSPC, short-write publication, concurrent partial writes, per-part concurrency, fsync EIO/retry and buffer/descriptor reads.
64-bit AddressSanitizer and UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer callback tests passed.
Format-501 integration passed: zeros, odd offsets, 512 KiB boundaries, split boundaries, partial physical tails, EOF, remounts, concurrent writes/fsync and loop-mounted ext4.
Formats 400 and 500 were rejected without modifying their fixture files.
Format-500 interoperability passed in both directions for the intermediate FUSE 3 build.
Format-501 interoperability passed in both directions between 32-bit static and 64-bit autotools builds.
All nine FAT32 matrix cases passed content/zero checks and all 36 fsck.fat checks passed.
One additional final-runner FAT32/XFS case passed after making fixture deletion contingent on successful unmount and fsck.
